notes.meaning: A simple dry crust eaten in peace brings far more contentment than a house filled with rich banquet meat and constant fighting. Lavish feasts often became occasions for selfish bickering and jealousy. A peaceful home with very little to eat is a far greater blessing than luxury paired with family conflict.

A trustworthy and sensible servant can end up ruling over a rebellious son who disgraces his family. That faithful worker may even be rewarded with a share of the family inheritance alongside the brothers. God honors genuine wisdom and good character over inherited privilege and status.

Metalworkers use hot pots and furnaces to melt down silver and gold, separating the pure metal from waste. In the same way, the Lord tests and purifies the human heart through trials and hardship. Only God can see past appearances to evaluate a person's true inner motives.

A wicked person pays close attention to malicious words, and a liar loves listening to slanderous talk. People who intend to do wrong naturally look for lies and rumors that support their bad plans. What someone enjoys listening to reveals what is really inside their heart.

Making fun of poor people insults the God who created them and placed them in the world. Laughing when other people suffer disaster also guarantees that God will judge the mocker. Believers must show compassion toward those who struggle instead of celebrating another person's downfall.

Grandchildren are like a glorious crown to their grandparents, marking a long life blessed with family. Children, in turn, take pride and comfort in having parents of good character and godly reputation. Each generation is designed to honor, support, and bless the other.

Eloquent, lofty speech sounds completely out of place coming from a vile and foolish person. It is even more improper and damaging when an honorable ruler or judge tells lies. Leaders bear a heavy responsibility to ensure their words match their high office and remain truthful.

To the person offering a bribe, the money looks like a dazzling gem that works wonders wherever he uses it. Corrupt gifts often succeed in swaying people in a broken world. While this proverb notes how effective bribery can be, it exposes the corrupt mindset of those who rely on money to bend justice.

A person who forgives a wrong and keeps it quiet nurtures love and keeps peace. On the other hand, someone who keeps bringing up past mistakes will destroy even a lifelong friendship. Choosing to overlook personal offenses is the best way to guard precious relationships.

A single word of gentle correction sinks deeper into a sensible person than a hundred lashes with a whip sink into a fool. A wise person has a tender conscience that responds quickly to truth. A stubborn fool hardens his heart, so even severe punishment fails to teach him anything.

An evil person is bent on rebellion against God and rightful authority, always looking for trouble. Because of this defiance, a severe messenger or judgment will be sent to punish him. Those who stubbornly resist all good guidance will eventually face strict justice.

It is safer to run into a fierce mother bear whose cubs have been stolen than to encounter a fool raging in his sin. An angry animal acts on raw instinct, but an ungodly fool acts with irrational malice and destructive pride. Staying far away from violent and reckless people prevents terrible harm.

Anyone who pays back good deeds with evil brings a curse of misery upon his own household. Returning kindness with cruelty is a terrible sin that overturns God's moral order. Showing deep gratitude toward those who help us protects our families from disaster.

Starting an argument is like making a tiny crack in a water dam that quickly bursts into an uncontrollable flood. What begins as a petty, sharp remark can rapidly tear a relationship apart. It is far better to stop a dispute right at the start before anger breaks loose.

Letting a guilty person go free and punishing an innocent person are both completely repulsive to the Lord. Civil rulers and judges are charged by God to defend the upright and punish evil. Any legal system that twists this duty opposes God's righteous character.

There is no point in a fool having money to pay for an education when he has no real desire to learn wisdom. Worldly wealth cannot buy good judgment for someone whose mind is closed to truth. Gaining true understanding requires humility and a willing heart, not just material resources.

A loyal friend loves through every season of life, whether in prosperity or in trouble. A true brother proves his value especially when hard times arrive, stepping in to carry the burden. Sincere friendship does not change when circumstances become difficult.

A person who lacks good sense quickly shakes hands on a deal and co-signs a neighbor's debt. Taking on another person's financial risk can bring financial ruin down upon one's own family. True charity helps friends in need without making foolish financial pledges.

A person who loves picking fights reveals a deep love for sin, because arguing stirs up pride and malice. In the same way, someone who builds an imposing, lofty gate shows arrogant boastfulness that invites his own downfall. Pride and conflict inevitably lead to ruin.

Anyone with a twisted, crooked heart will never find true happiness or God's favor. Likewise, a person who tells lies and talks deceitfully will stumble straight into trouble. Dishonesty and inner wickedness always undermine the person practicing them.

A man who fathers a rebellious, foolish child brings heavy grief upon himself. Such a father finds no joy in his offspring, watching his hopes turn into heartbreak. Raising children to fear the Lord is vital for the peace and comfort of the home.

A cheerful heart filled with peace acts like healing medicine for the physical body. In contrast, deep sorrow and a crushed spirit wear down a person's vitality and dry out the bones. Cultivating gladness in God protects both spiritual and physical health.

A wicked person secretly accepts a bribe hidden inside his clothing so he can twist the outcome of justice. Taking secret money corrupts judges and denies justice to the innocent. God condemns any hidden dealings that pervert what is fair and right.

A discerning person keeps wisdom right in front of him as his steady goal and guide for daily living. In contrast, a fool's eyes roam aimlessly toward the ends of the earth, chasing wild dreams and endless distractions. Keeping your focus on God's truth protects you from wasting your life.

A foolish child causes sharp grief to his father and bitter sorrow to the mother who gave him birth. Rebellious living disregards the loving care and hard work parents poured out for their child. Honoring parents by living wisely brings comfort to the whole household.

It is thoroughly wrong to fine or punish an innocent person in a court of law. It is just as evil to beat honorable leaders simply because they did what was right and fair. Leaders must use their power to defend righteousness rather than persecute upright people.

A person with true knowledge is careful with his words, choosing when to speak and when to remain quiet. Someone with genuine understanding keeps a calm, cool spirit even when provoked. Mastering your temper and tongue shows real maturity.

Even an ignorant fool is thought to be wise if he simply keeps his mouth closed. When he holds his tongue, people assume he is exercising thoughtful restraint. Learning to stay silent prevents many embarrassing mistakes and shields a person from trouble.
